rachel_cs: Heads-up  onboarding for BlueCove is hitting a wall. Their QA runs show a burst of 200s on init then a concentrated window of 429s right after the ephemeral token swap. Theyre on browser-sdk v0.9.2 behind a corporate proxy. Any quick triage suggestions? :thinking:

diego_sdk: That pattern screams token-rotation stampede + possible proxy replay. How many parallel warmups do they do on first load?

rachel_cs: They said they spawn 10 parallel workers that each call embeddings + chat warmup. Their log snippet:
```
2026-06-12T09:15:30Z INFO ephemeral_refresh ok user=bluecove id=bv-101 ttl=60s
2026-06-12T09:15:31Z WARN http status=429 x-request-id=bc-2001 attempts=3
2026-06-12T09:15:32Z WARN http status=429 x-request-id=bc-2002 attempts=4
```
They also mentioned the proxy sometimes resets keepalives and can replay requests when clients retry.

amy_ops: If the proxy replays retries we can see amplified bursts even with modest concurrency. Two quick asks for the customer: 1) in a dev environment, reduce client concurrency and 2) add randomized splay on the token refresh path.

diego_sdk: To keep wording different from past threads, ask them to try SDK option `initConcurrency: 3` (instead of our more commonly suggested flag) and a refresh splay of 150-450ms. Also confirm the SDK isn't disabled from performing jitter/backoff.

kevin_eng: If they cant change prod fast, we can offer a short-lived platform tweak: increase ephemeral TTL from 60s -> 180s for a 12-24 hour window and enable per-route smoothing (a soft shed that spaces preflight attempts). Operational risk: longer-lived tokens means broader blast radius for leaked tokens; document and timebox. Need CS + ops approval.

rachel_cs: I drafted a small playbook and asked BlueCove whether they want us to try the platform tweak first or run the client repro. They asked us to prepare the playbook before they pick.

amy_ops: Playbook diagnostic steps for ops to verify root cause:
1) Grep our ingress logs for the API key and collect `x-request-id` series:
```
grep "x-request-id" /var/log/redwood/ingress.log | grep <api_key> | head -n 200
```
2) Check `x-ratewindow` header patterns and group by IP to see if burst originates from single IP or many:
```
awk '/x-ratewindow/ {print $0}' /var/log/redwood/ingress.log | grep <api_key> | sort | uniq -c
```
3) If single IP -> proxy likely replaying; if multiple IPs -> multi-tab/workers client-side. Also inspect whether Authorization headers are duplicated or rewritten by the proxy.

kevin_eng: For the platform tweak procedure (ops):
- Preflight: snapshot current TTL and smoothing flags for the key; capture baseline 429 rate.
- Change: set ephemeral ttl=180s and enable per-route smoothing for the key during low-traffic window.
- Monitor: watch 429 rate, token-reuse alerts, and auth anomalies for 2x the expected rotation interval.
- Rollback: revert ttl and smoothing flags after 12-24h or earlier if anomalies detected.
Include automated rollback job so ops can revert quickly.

rachel_cs: I posted the playbook in the ticket BCV-3102 and asked BlueCove if they prefer client patch first or immediate platform smoothing. Also linked monitoring: https://console.redwood.example/account/bluecove/keys/bcv-101/metrics

ticket-bot: Note added to BCV-3102 by rachel_cs  "investigating token-rotation 429 window; proposed client splay + initConcurrency change, offered temporary TTL=180s + per-route smoothing; awaiting customer decision"

diego_sdk: One more diagnostic pointer for them to run in staging: spin up a small script that simulates N tabs and logs timestamps of token refresh + first requests. If requests line up within a 100-500ms window, that confirms stampede. Sample pseudo:
```
for i in 1..8 do & Redw.init({ initConcurrency: 3, tokenSplayMs: 250 })
```

rachel_cs: BlueCove prefers the platform tweak for speed. I asked ops to schedule the change for midnight UTC and to enable strict monitoring. Will update the thread after the smoothing test. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
